reason: Connect the methane line to its matching store as a first step toward filling the flight tank.
expectation: I expect a methane transfer connection, perhaps still needing attachment to the lander.

alternatives.reason: The oxygen line also needs connecting; I picked methane first without a strong preference.

effect: The matching line and store formed an assembly, which can now be used at the methane tank.
reason: Finish the methane transfer before setting up oxygen.
expectation: The assembly should connect to and fill the methane tank, though a further check may be needed.

alternatives.reason: I could prepare the oxygen line first, but prefer to complete one path at a time.

effect: The methane tank is filled, leaving the oxygen path to set up.
reaction: A small, straightforward sense of progress.
reason: Prepare the matching oxygen line and store; it is the only gameplay option.
expectation: I expect an oxygen transfer assembly analogous to the methane one.

effect: The oxygen assembly is ready for its tank, just like methane.
reaction: The parallel sequence is clear but repetitive.
reason: Fill the oxygen tank with the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: I expect a filled oxygen tank and completion of the goal.

effect: Both separate flight tanks are now filled and the goal is complete.
reaction: It is reassuring to complete the return preparation, though the outcome was expected.

mostWorthwhile.text: Filling the methane tank gave a concrete payoff to the long-running fuel production and made progress toward return feel tangible.

leastWorthwhile.text: The oxygen assembly and transfer repeated the methane sequence with little new information or choice.

surprise.text: Nothing in this chapter particularly surprised me; each matching line and tank behaved as expected.

arbitrary.text: No action lacked a clear purpose: matching each certified line to its liquid and tank made sense. The order between the paths felt inconsequential.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue to see how the discovered body and its surrounding ice make the journey home; this short chapter itself was more procedural than compelling.
